body: Indian shareholding disclosures only show holders with >=1% of a company, filed quarterly (typically within ~3 weeks of quarter-end), so a follower sees entries 1-4 months late, never sees sub-1% holdings, and usually learns of exits only after the next filing. Media 'X buys Y' stories routinely move small caps 5-20% on the news (observed pattern; magnitude unverified), so the follower's entry price is worse than the investor's. Superstar books are large and diversified (Mukul Agrawal ~72 stocks, Kacholia ~45-49, Dolly Khanna ~12-20 frequently churned), so any single disclosed stock may be a 0.5% experiment for them but a 20% bet for you. Survivorship: lists of 'superstar multibaggers' omit the many holdings that fell 50%+ in 2018-19 and 2025. Pabrai's cloning works better because he clones concentrated, long-held positions of investors with published reasoning, and still applies his own checklist. Useful use: treat disclosed stakes as a pre-screened idea list; check the investor's average cost (bulk-deal or filing prices), the stock's governance and valuation now, and size by your conviction, not theirs.

data.lesson: use as idea source, not signal; check lag, size and price paid

title: Cloning Indian 'superstar' portfolios: why it usually underdelivers
